statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-64847 (GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp): AnyIO starts process-pool workers with stderr connected to a pipe that is never drained, so worker code that writes enough attacker-influenced data to stderr can block the worker and wedge the awaiting process-pool call. It affects anyio 4.14.1 and earlier and is fixed in 4.14.2, where commit f1b7301 ("Fixed stderr writes in a worker subprocess causing a deadlock", #1207) redirects the worker's stderr to /dev/null in anyio/to_process.py (https://github.com/agronholm/anyio/security/advisories/GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp, https://github.com/agronholm/anyio/commit/f1b7301c8264b0d2e8d24a5788fd29e93dea4040). Listed the files of all 100 published airflow packages in the DHI Debian repository, 3.3.0-0 to the current 3.4.0-9 (50 builds, amd64 and arm64; no debug-symbol packages are published for this source), including the members of the wheel and jar archives inside them, and read the anyio version from its dist-info metadata under /usr/lib/airflow/lib/python3.13/site-packages; both architectures agree for every build, and no other copy of anyio (a second dist-info directory, a vendored package directory or an embedded wheel) is present in any build. Builds 3.3.0-0 to 3.3.0-3 ship anyio 4.14.1, whose anyio/to_process.py has the same size as the one in the 4.14.1 release on PyPI, which lacks the stderr redirect. From 3.3.1-0 every build ships a fixed release: 4.14.2 in 3.3.1-0 to 3.3.1-15, 4.15.1 in 3.3.2-0 to 3.3.2-19, and 4.16.0 in 3.4.0-0 to 3.4.0-9. Unpacking 3.4.0-9 for amd64 and arm64 showed the stderr redirect in to_process.py. So 3.3.1-0 is the first fixed build.
